items.text: Sequence matters more than speed.
The resume gap is rarely the dealbreaker it feels like.
A layoff is not a referendum on your worth or your skill.

blocks.heading: Real, and It Is Not Weakness

items.text: Skipping this section would be dishonest.
A layoff can genuinely feel like losing a piece of your identity, even when you know intellectually that it was a company decision and not a personal failure.
A rough daily routine, even a simple one, protects your mood and your discipline far more than an open, unstructured day does.
This is the single most consequential decision in a layoff restart, and most people make it under pressure instead of on purpose.
If your honest energy for the work was fading before the layoff, chasing an identical role elsewhere just delays a decision you were already circling.
Confusing grief over the job loss with genuine desire to stay in the same field is a common mix-up.

blocks.heading: Turn a Layoff Into a Lost Year

items.text: Scattershot applications to unrelated roles waste interview slots and confuse your own positioning.
A vague or evasive answer about a layoff reads worse than a short, honest one.
Watching your runway shrink to almost nothing before widening your search or lowering your target compensation puts you in the worst negotiating position possible.

blocks.heading: Financial Triage Before Job Search
rows: Add up cash, liquid mutual funds, and fixed deposits. Divide by your true monthly non-negotiable spend (EMIs, rent, food, insurance, school fees). That number of months is your runway, not a guess, a fact you can plan around.
Full and final settlement, gratuity if you cross the eligibility period, leave encashment, and any pending bonus or variable pay. This is money already earned, not a favour from your former employer.
Pause, do not panic-stop, your investments

A SIP running on zero income is not discipline, it is a hole in your runway. Pause it, keep the mandate active, and restart once income resumes, do not redeem long-term investments unless the runway math forces it.
Talk to lenders before you miss a payment
Banks and NBFCs increasingly offer moratoriums or restructuring for a genuine job loss. A call before a missed EMI protects your credit score; a call after does not undo the damage as easily.

items.text: 01 Was your role automatable, or was it your specific employer's cost-cutting.
List your last year of tasks honestly.
Most professionals can name one skill gap honestly within a minute of being asked directly.

blocks.heading: Gap on Your Resume and in Interviews

items.text: Vague dates or a resume that quietly stretches the last role's end date.
Visibly bitter or critical language about the previous employer.
A long, over-explained story that sounds rehearsed and defensive.
1 Do the money math and claim your dues.
2 Run the skill gap audit and the four questions.
3 Rebuild your resume and one clean explanation of the gap.
4 Reactivate your network before you touch job portals.
5 Run both channels in parallel: referrals and direct applications.
6 Review and adjust at a pace that fits your runway.
Global data suggests a majority of laid-off professionals find a new role within roughly three months, while the overall average, pulled up by longer searches, tends to run several months longer.
A meaningful share of laid-off workers submit well over fifty applications, and some over a hundred, before landing an offer, volume alone is rarely the fast path.

In India specifically, referral-led and direct-conversation hiring fills a large share of professional roles, which is part of why a deliberately reactivated network tends to shorten the search more than blind applications do.
